expectation: I expect the directed builders to join the amino acids into collagen or an early form of it.

reason: Adding the new fibers to the body should help rebuild support at the scrape.

expectation: I expect the signals to prompt the skin cells to help cover the scrape, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: The signals influence skin cells to move and multiply, providing coverage using materials and energy. The spreading cells can now be added to the rebuilding body.

reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should restore surface coverage over the scrape.

effect: Surface coverage is restored, while deeper rebuilding continues and the patch may retain a scar.
reaction: The ending ties the cellular work back to the whole body, though the repair is less tidy than a complete reset.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supporting fibers was most worthwhile: it connected protein production inside cells to the material supporting tissue outside them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the finished fibers to the body felt predictable after the preceding construction, although it made the change at the scrape clear.

surprise.text: I was interested that cells make collagen material that is processed outside them into fibers forming part of their surroundings.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The offered combinations had clear purposes, though the final two were the only combinations available.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter if it explored a new body process. The connection between cell work and tissue repair held my interest, though some steps were predictable.
